newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Dominican Republic leader removes military chief.
newsitem.headline: Dominican Republic leader removes military chief.

text.p: President Leonel Fernandez of the Dominican Republic has removed his military chief, just days after appointing him, in a move to stifle discontent in the upper ranks of the armed forces.

Fernandez announced in a nationwide speech on Friday night that he had dismissed Armed Forces Secretary Lieutenant General Juan Bautista Rojas Tabar and three other generals, including the navy chief and the commander of an important army brigade.

Fernandez appointed General Ruben Paulino Alvarez as head of the armed forces. He promoted Francisco Frias Olivencia from vice admiral to admiral and handed him command of the navy in place of Vice Admiral Gerardo Santana Solano.
Generals Ramon Alcide Rodriiguez Arias of the police and Fernando Sanchez Aybar of the army, both of whom held important positons under Balaguer, were also retired.

The move came one day after Rojas Tabar demanded the dismissal of several generals, saying he would retire himself otherwise. He had only held the position since Monday, when his predecessor was removed.

The Dominican military has been in a state of agitation this week following the reopening of an investigation into the disappearance in 1994 of leftist university professor and journalist Narcisco Gonzalez.
Gonzalez, a vocal opponent of the previous government of Joaquin Balaguer, was kidnapped in May 1994 and his familiy believes he was murdered by the military.
Rojas Tabar on Thursday appeared voluntarily before the attorney general, Abel Rodriguez del Orbe, for questioning on the case.
He said other senior officers were trying to smear his name by implicating him in it. He said either they should go or he would.

Fernandez expressed "respect and sympathy for the courage and valour shown by General Rojas Tabar in defence of his honour. But I cannot permit, under any circumstances, that any member of the armed forces or police makes demands of me in front of the people in a dispute of this nature."
Fernandez, who won power from strongman Balaguer in elections in May, said he wanted to stop the disorder that had existed in the country for more than three decades.
He also intended to clear up the Gonzalez case.
Rojas Tabar's comments had generated tensions in barracks but the president's speech seemed to have restored discipline, a high-placed military sorce told Reuters.
"All the retired officers have accepted the president's decision. He is our commander in chief," the source said.
Fernandez on Monday retired 24 generals, including Constantino Matos Villanueva, who was armed forces secretary when Gonzalez disappeared.
The government said the generals, most of whom were close to Balaguer, were retired to trim the top-heavy military and cut state expenses.
Matos Villanueva was banned from leaving the country pending the probe into the disappearance. He has protested his innocence.
